items.question: What form is to be contemplated as seated and adorned with white ornaments?
premises: The form is seated in that place.
It is adorned with white ornaments.
items.inference: The meditator should visualize the adorned seated form.
uncertainties: Exact sandhi of tasmiṃścaiva not expanded.
items.plain_english: In that place, seated and adorned with white ornaments.

items.question: How should the adorned form be ritually treated during remembrance?
premises: It is sprinkled with milk-water and all substances.
One should remember it.
items.inference: Remembrance includes sprinkling the form with milk-water and all substances.
items.plain_english: One should remember it being sprinkled with milk-water and all substances.

items.question: What arises when the form plays with varied enjoyments?
premises: It plays with various enjoyments.
A wish-form becomes.
items.inference: The wish-form arises from the play of varied enjoyments.
uncertainties: Exact relation of icchārūpa to krīḍate.
items.plain_english: It plays with various enjoyments, and a wish-form becomes.

items.question: What is meditated upon after striking above by the moon?
premises: One meditates on the moon-seat-seated form.
It is struck above by the moon.
items.inference: The meditated form is the moon-seat-seated one struck above by the moon.
items.plain_english: Having meditated on the moon-seat-seated form struck above by the moon.

items.question: What qualities characterize the form freed from old age and death?
premises: It is freed from old age and death.
It is devoid of all disease.
items.inference: The form is both free from aging and death and free from all disease.
items.plain_english: Freed from old age and death, devoid of all disease.

items.question: What does the speaker ask the goddess to hear next?
premises: Another wonderful thing is introduced.
The goddess is asked to hear.
items.inference: The goddess is invited to hear another wonderful teaching.
items.plain_english: Hear another wonderful thing, O goddess, O family-minded one.

items.question: What happens to old age and disease when this is meditated upon?
premises: This is being meditated upon.
Old age and disease are destroyed.
items.inference: Meditation on this destroys old age and disease.
items.plain_english: When this is meditated upon, O goddess, old age and disease are destroyed.

items.question: Where should this moon be meditated upon?
premises: One should meditate on this moon.
It is in navel-head and heart-gone.
items.inference: The moon is meditated in the navel-head and heart region.
items.plain_english: One should meditate on this moon, O goddess, in navel-head and heart.

items.question: What is attained after this meditation?
premises: Then independence is attained.
It is devoid of old age and death.
items.inference: The practitioner attains independence free from old age and death.
items.plain_english: Then one attains independence devoid of old age and death.

items.question: How is the thousand-petaled form described?
premises: It is endowed with thousand-petal beauty.
It resembles cow-milk whiteness.
items.inference: The form is thousand-petaled and white like cow's milk.
items.plain_english: Endowed with thousand-petal beauty, resembling cow's milk whiteness.

items.question: What happens to the form mounted below by the wheel above?
premises: It is mounted below by the wheel.
It is flooded by the wheel above.
items.inference: The form is flooded above while mounted below by the wheel.
items.plain_english: Mounted below by the wheel, flooded by the wheel above.

items.question: What bodily afflictions are removed in this result?
premises: It is freed from wrinkles and grey hair.
It is devoid of all disease.
items.inference: The result removes wrinkles, grey hair, and all disease.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, devoid of all disease.
